sourceTrace.notes: C-023 is the sole owner for a patient who suspects a defect in childbirth care but does not yet have the complete medical record or a medical conclusion on causation. The source is a BPU demand signal, not confirmed paid work, an established medical error or a successful case. R-0097 and R-0098 provide client language; P-011 supports the evidence-before-claim sequence.

intentOwnership.intent: пациент после родов подозревает дефект медицинской помощи и ищет правильную доказательственную последовательность

intentOwnership.reason: Existing publications do not cover medical records, quality expertise, causation and the first legal steps after a suspected childbirth-related medical error.

experimentException.reason: The owner explicitly ordered development of the next article. Direct confirmed five-result organic snapshots separately from Yandex and Google were not obtained; publication is therefore a measured experiment without fabricated SERP data.
experimentException.successCriteria: Relevant organic impressions and substantive reading, or at least one qualified inquiry about obtaining medical records, quality expertise, a possible medical error during childbirth or compensation for health damage.
experimentException.failureCriteria: After 90 days with healthy indexation, there are no relevant impressions, substantive reading or qualified inquiries.

practicalElements.title: Как связать симптомы, действия врачей и последствия
practicalElements.userValue: Separates the symptom, expected response, actual response, supporting document, consequence and expert question, helping the patient distinguish an adverse outcome from a provable defect in care.
practicalElements.competitorGap: Typical explanations jump from a bad outcome to an expert examination or compensation demand without showing which medical records are needed, how to separate several medical organizations and how to formulate causation questions.
practicalElements.sourceBasis: C-023, dialog 68d7acdf-f74c-8332-b8e0-6487c38f5775, R-0097, R-0098, P-011, Articles 22, 37, 64 and 98 of Federal Law 323-FZ, Article 40 of Federal Law 326-FZ, Order 789n, Articles 1064, 1085 and 208 of the Civil Code, Constitutional Court ruling 4-P and Supreme Court Plenum ruling 33.
